ai.description: This 20–25 mm frog is brown with dark mottling and a distinct pale mid-dorsal stripe. It features a pointed snout, granular skin, and lacks webbing between its fingers.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Raorchestes kaikatti* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, dark-colored "X" or hourglass-shaped marking on its dorsum, which is absent in similar congeners.
ai.habitat: The Kaikatti Bush Frog inhabits high-altitude shola forests and montane grasslands in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations above 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Kaikatti bush frog is strictly nocturnal, spending its nights foraging for small insects among the leaf litter and low-lying vegetation of its forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: The Kaikatti bush frog exhibits direct development, bypassing the tadpole stage. It breeds during the monsoon, laying small clutches of eggs in leaf axils or tree holes.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Kaikatti Bush Frog is endemic to the high-elevation shola forests and grasslands of the Anamalai Hills in the Western Ghats, specifically within Kerala and Tamil Nadu.
ai.callDescription: The Kaikatti Bush Frog emits a series of high-pitched, insect-like chirps, typically heard from vegetation within high-altitude shola forests.
